seo_title: Cost of Living in Madrid 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Madrid per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The capital of Spain at the heart of the country: a rich cultural life, excellent gastronomy and developed infrastructure. Russian citizens need a visa (a nomad visa works); it's pricier than the coast, with hot summers and a winter that's cool for the south.
pros: Capital-city cultural life and world-class museums
Convenient transport and connections across Europe
A safe and comfortable city to live in
cons: Hot summers and a cool winter (no sea nearby)
NIE bureaucracy and queues for cita previa

visa_steps.title: Visa
visa_steps.description: Russians need a Schengen or national visa (for example, a nomad visa).

visa_steps.title: NIE
visa_steps.description: A foreigner's identification number — needed for almost every procedure.

visa_steps.title: Registration (empadronamiento)
visa_steps.description: Registering your place of residence at the district town hall.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Spanish banks open accounts once you have a NIE and an address.

visa_steps.title: Residence permit (TIE)
visa_steps.description: The resident card is issued after arrival on a long-term visa.

faq.question: Do Russians need a visa for Madrid?
faq.answer: Yes, you need a Schengen or national visa — Spain is in the Schengen area.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Madrid?
faq.answer: Pricier than the coast, but cheaper than Paris and London. See the exact budget in the calculator above.

faq.question: What language is spoken in Madrid?
faq.answer: Spanish; English is common in tourism and among young people.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Madrid?
faq.answer: No, Russian cards don't work. You need a foreign bank card or euros in cash.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Madrid?
faq.answer: Continental: hot, dry summers and a cool, sometimes snowy winter — there's no sea nearby.

faq.question: Is Madrid suitable for remote work?
faq.answer: Yes, there's Spain's nomad visa; the city is loved for its culture, transport and infrastructure.

reviews.text: Madrid is museums, tapas and easy living in the centre of Europe. I got the nomad visa. The downsides — NIE bureaucracy and the fact there's no sea nearby.
A lively, cultural, safe city with great food. Hot in summer, cool in winter. The main hurdle for Russians is getting the visa and getting through all the cita previa.
